claims.statement: For each eligible instance and the one fixed original strict favorable-leaf selector F(T,p), the aggregate has the exact weighted-layer representation S=sum_{B in I_(p+1)(T)} w_F(B)-sum_{A in I_p(T)} w_F(A), where w_F(B) counts selected original leaf tags v in B with (B\{v}) intersect W_v nonempty. On the actual finite one-vertex deletion graph between these independent-set layers, a saturating integral flow with upper supplies w_F and lower capacities w_F exists exactly when every deletion-neighborhood cut X satisfies sum_X w_F <= sum_{N_-(X)}w_F; any such flow certifies S<=0. This is an instancewise reduction only; the universal cut inequalities and primary aggregate remain unproved.
claims.scope: Narrowed to the algebraic fixed-selector identity and its finite-instance weighted max-flow/min-cut equivalence for ordinary trees under x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, using original supports/neighborhoods and counting same-support leaves with multiplicity. It does not assert the universal cuts or a universal sign theorem.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the tagwise enlargement/deletion bijection, summand rank identity, and integer-capacity min-cut argument are valid, including zero supply and repeated supports. The full-layer cut is exactly S<=0, while the route establishes neither that cut nor all proper cuts for every eligible tree and provides no concrete instance. Thus it supports only the exact reduction and conditional certificate criterion, not a proof or refutation of the registered universal aggregate.

limitations: No universal weighted deletion-cut proof or eligible cut failure is supplied.
